learning_objective: The learner will judge how to resolve each of five disagreements between two reviewers by choosing the resolution that their evidence supports, with at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** score-reconciliation-judge
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge how to resolve each of five disagreements between two reviewers by choosing the resolution that their evidence supports, with at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Consensus Scoring, Score Reconciliation, Evidence Recording, Inter-Rater Agreement (defined in Chapter 3) (all defined in this chapter or in Chapter 3 above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each case the learner commits one of four resolutions. A resolution is correct when it matches the Correct resolution column in Content. Mastery is at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt. Reading the three-step procedure is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Average the two scores. (2) The more senior reviewer's score wins. (3) A tool report settles any score. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging between two reviewers' evidence is an Evaluate-level action. Five cases in which different kinds of evidence meet teach the learner to ask which evidence is specific, which is repeatable, and which belongs to the check. **Content:** The four resolutions: Reviewer A's score stands, Reviewer B's score stands, Re-check and decide, Record the disagreement. The three-step procedure, shown on request: each reviewer states their evidence; the reviewers repeat the check the evidence rests on; they choose the score the checked evidence supports. The five cases (all made up, for Watershed Basics): | # | Metric | Reviewer A | Reviewer B | Correct resolution | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Accessibility | Score 5. Evidence: "4 of 5 images have alt text, and 2 of those 4 are one word. The video has no captions. One heading skips a level." | Score 9. Evidence: "An automated checker reported no errors." | Reviewer A's score stands | A's evidence is specific and repeatable. A checker cannot judge alt text quality or the absence of captions, so B's evidence does not address A's findings. | | 2 | Portability | Score 7. Evidence: "The embed worked on 2 of 3 test platforms and failed on the third, tested 2026-10-12." | Score 3. Evidence: "It did not work in my LMS." | Re-check and decide | B's evidence names no platform, no date, and no cause, and it may point at the same failure A found or at a new one. Repeat the test on B's platform. | | 3 | Open license | Score 3. Evidence: "I found no license." | Score 9. Evidence: "CC BY 4.0 appears in the footer of pages 1 to 6, with a link to the license." | Reviewer B's score stands | B's evidence is specific and shows that A missed the footer. | | 4 | Modularity | Score 5. Evidence: "The quiz cannot be opened apart from the reading, and it has no address of its own." | Score 9. Evidence: "The reading is divided into sections with clear headings." | Reviewer A's score stands | Headings divide a page and do not make the parts separable, so B's evidence answers a different question. | | 5 | Practice with feedback | Score 8. Evidence: "All 8 items give feedback after the learner clicks Show answer." | Score 4. Evidence: "The feedback appears only after the click on Show answer, so it is not immediate." | Record the disagreement | Both readings are defensible, because the rubric does not say whether click-to-reveal counts as feedback after the learner responds. Record the disagreement and ask the rubric's owner to clarify the check. | **Provenance:** The cases are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The procedure follows the chapter section "Score Reconciliation". **Rules:** Each case has exactly one correct resolution. Two cases are Reviewer A's score stands, one is Reviewer B's score stands, one is Re-check and decide, and one is Record the disagreement. The sim never offers averaging as a resolution, and states that averaging is not a resolution. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the metric, both reviewers' scores, and both reviewers' evidence. 2. The learner may open the three-step procedure. Opening it does not change the score. 3. The learner chooses a resolution, and the choice is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After case 5 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 5 cases in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [resolution]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The best resolution is [resolution]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 5 correct on the first attempt". At 4 or more it adds "You can settle a disagreement with evidence." Below 4 it lists the Why text of each missed case. **Starting State:** Case 1 with both reviewers' scores and evidence shown. The question shown is "How should these two reviewers resolve this metric?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says reconciliation applies when scores differ by more than 3 points, that the reviewers decide by evidence and never average, and that unresolved metrics are recorded as disputed.
